title: Bowel obstruction and ileus in the hospital
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the bowel obstruction or ileus (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/18/2026
Reason for Admission: Acute abdominal pain and vomiting.

Vitals:
Temperature: 98.6 F
Blood Pressure: 132/84 mmHg
Heart Rate: 82 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
Oxygen Saturation: 98% on room air

Recent Labs:
WBC: 11.4 x 10^9/L
Hemoglobin: 12.2 g/dL
Hematocrit: 37%
Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL
eGFR: 72 mL/min/1.73m2
Electrolytes: Sodium 138 mEq/L, Potassium 4.0 mEq/L

Review of Systems:
The patient reports significant abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. She denies fever, chills, chest pain, or shortness of breath. She reports no changes in bowel habits prior to admission.

Social History:
The patient is a retired school teacher who lives with her spouse. She does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally.

Family History:
Mother had hypertension. Father had a history of coronary artery disease.

Hospital Course:
The patient is a 77-year-old female who presented to the emergency department with severe abdominal distension and inability to pass gas. Physical examination and imaging confirmed a complete small bowel obstruction. The underlying etiology was determined to be adhesions resulting from a previous abdominal surgery. The patient was stabilized with intravenous fluids and nasogastric tube decompression. Due to the severity of the symptoms, she underwent a surgical release of adhesions. The procedure was successful, and the bowel was decompressed. Postoperatively, she remained stable, with improving abdominal pain and tolerance of oral liquids. She was transitioned to a regular diet and was discharged in stable condition.

Discharge Diagnoses:
Complete small bowel obstruction due to adhesions.

Discharge Medications:
1. Acetaminophen 650mg every 6 hours as needed for pain.
2. Ondansetron 4mg as needed for nausea.

Follow-up:
The patient will follow up with her primary care physician in one week for a routine check-up and to monitor her recovery from the surgery.

Electronically signed, E. Castillo, MD, 05/18/2026
explanations: Intestinal adhesions with complete obstruction: K56.52 (HCC 78).
